probabilityOfWeed.notes: Berkeley has a handful of licensed dispensaries and was an early medical-cannabis city. Adult use has been legal in California since 2016 (Prop 64) for anyone 21+ with ID; buy only from shops or delivery services licensed by the state Department of Cannabis Control, and don't smoke in public places. Federal law still bans cannabis: for a non-citizen, using, buying or working with it, even legally under state law, can count against a visa, green card or citizenship application, and it must never cross a state or national border. Safest for Winnie: skip it.

fashionEcosystem.clothingMfg: Mostly independent makers and home sewists; Stonemountain's classes are the community hub.
fashionEcosystem.fabricSourcing: Stonemountain & Daughter for linen and cottons, the Lacis Museum shop for lace and embroidery supplies, ImagiKnit for yarn; A Verb for Keeping Warm is ten minutes away in Oakland.
fashionEcosystem.vintageThrift: Crossroads Trading on Shattuck, Telegraph Avenue's student-vintage shops, and the Alameda antiques faire nearby.
fashionEcosystem.danceTheatre: Cal Performances' world dance seasons, Ashkenaz's dance nights (Afro-Caribbean, Balkan, Brazilian and more), Berkeley Rep and Shotgun Players for theatre.

trimWorkOpportunities.season: Sep-Nov (outdoor harvest on the North Coast)
trimWorkOpportunities.notes: Not a route for Winnie. Licensed farms in Humboldt, Mendocino and Trinity counties hire harvest and trim crews in autumn, but only workers with US work authorization, and because cannabis is still illegal under federal law, cannabis work can harm a visa or immigration case even on a state-licensed farm. Unlicensed cash trimming is illegal and often unsafe. Any paid work in the US, in any industry, needs work authorization.

probabilityOfWeed.notes: Oakland was an early centre of the legal industry and has many licensed dispensaries. Adult use has been legal in California since 2016 (Prop 64) for anyone 21+ with ID; buy only from shops or delivery services licensed by the state Department of Cannabis Control, and don't smoke in public places. Federal law still bans cannabis: for a non-citizen, using, buying or working with it, even legally under state law, can count against a visa, green card or citizenship application, and it must never cross a state or national border. Safest for Winnie: skip it.

fashionEcosystem.clothingMfg: Independent designers and small sewing studios in West Oakland and downtown warehouses; no large garment district.
fashionEcosystem.fabricSourcing: A Verb for Keeping Warm for natural dye, yarn and fabric; East Bay Depot for Creative Reuse for cheap materials; Bay Quilts in Richmond for cottons; Stonemountain in Berkeley.
fashionEcosystem.vintageThrift: Crossroads Trading on College Avenue, Out of the Closet, and the Alameda Point Antiques Faire (first Sunday monthly) for vintage cloth.
fashionEcosystem.danceTheatre: Oakland Ballet, Destiny Arts Center (youth dance and arts), Diamano Coura West African Dance Company and AXIS Dance Company (physically integrated dance).

trimWorkOpportunities.season: Sep-Nov (outdoor harvest on the North Coast)
trimWorkOpportunities.notes: Not a route for Winnie. Licensed farms in Humboldt, Mendocino and Trinity counties hire harvest and trim crews in autumn, but only workers with US work authorization, and because cannabis is still illegal under federal law, cannabis work can harm a visa or immigration case even on a state-licensed farm. Unlicensed cash trimming is illegal and often unsafe. Any paid work in the US, in any industry, needs work authorization.

probabilityOfWeed.notes: Marin has very few cannabis storefronts; licensed delivery is the usual route. Check San Rafael's current rules. Adult use has been legal in California since 2016 (Prop 64) for anyone 21+ with ID; buy only from shops or delivery services licensed by the state Department of Cannabis Control, and don't smoke in public places. Federal law still bans cannabis: for a non-citizen, using, buying or working with it, even legally under state law, can count against a visa, green card or citizenship application, and it must never cross a state or national border. Safest for Winnie: skip it.

fashionEcosystem.clothingMfg: Small independent makers; Fibershed (Point Reyes Station, 40 min) connects local farmers, dyers and sewists.
fashionEcosystem.fabricSourcing: Dharma Trading is a national dye supplier right here (natural dyes, mordants, undyed silk and cotton); Atelier Yarns downtown for yarn and weaving tools.
fashionEcosystem.vintageThrift: Charity and consignment shops downtown; bigger vintage in San Francisco and Oakland.
fashionEcosystem.danceTheatre: Marin Theatre (Mill Valley), the Mountain Play, and dance and music at the Marin Center.

places.name: Dharma Trading Co.

places.name: Atelier Yarns

trimWorkOpportunities.season: Sep-Nov (outdoor harvest on the North Coast)
trimWorkOpportunities.notes: Not a route for Winnie. Licensed farms in Humboldt, Mendocino and Trinity counties hire harvest and trim crews in autumn, but only workers with US work authorization, and because cannabis is still illegal under federal law, cannabis work can harm a visa or immigration case even on a state-licensed farm. Unlicensed cash trimming is illegal and often unsafe. Any paid work in the US, in any industry, needs work authorization.

probabilityOfWeed.status: Recreational legal (21+); no storefronts in Palo Alto
probabilityOfWeed.notes: Palo Alto bans cannabis businesses in town other than deliveries from licensed services elsewhere. Adult use has been legal in California since 2016 (Prop 64) for anyone 21+ with ID; buy only from shops or delivery services licensed by the state Department of Cannabis Control, and don't smoke in public places. Federal law still bans cannabis: for a non-citizen, using, buying or working with it, even legally under state law, can count against a visa, green card or citizenship application, and it must never cross a state or national border. Safest for Winnie: skip it.

fashionEcosystem.clothingMfg: Very little; this is tech country. Makerspaces (Maker Nexus in Sunnyvale) have sewing machines and laser cutters.
fashionEcosystem.fabricSourcing: No major fabric store verified nearby; Britex (San Francisco) and Stonemountain (Berkeley) are about an hour. The Black Sheep Handweavers Guild meets in Redwood City.
fashionEcosystem.vintageThrift: Charity thrift shops in Palo Alto, Menlo Park and Mountain View.
